/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]

Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: The grant has to be an exact `files_touched:` block in the body of this issue. `.github/workflows/implement.yml` (lines 1648–1658) passes the issue metadata snapshot to `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py --emit-automation-grant`, and that script's `extract_files_touched` (lines 110–140) reads only the first `files_touched:` block in the body. A `/answer` comment therefore can't supply the grant. Option A covers both automation paths the #6785 run staged, plus the ordinary files the guard checks once a list exists. It's also the only option that lets the repo variable turn the flag on per repository. Option C repeats the #6785 rejection. Option B leaves the flag with no way to be switched on until another PR.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/implement.yml:1648-1664: the grant is emitted from the issue body plus the issue author (`--pipeline-login`, OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR).
    - scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:110-140: the block format is a line `files_touched:` followed by more-indented `- <path>` lines, with no blank line inside the list.
    - Existing targets: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh, .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml, tests/test_check_failure_triage_workflow_security.py.
    - New file: changelog.d/6785-check-triage-pr-head-routing.md
  steps:
    - Before implement runs, the issue body must contain exactly this block (2-space indented entries):
        files_touched:
          - scripts/check_failure_triage.sh
          - .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml
          - tests/test_check_failure_triage_workflow_security.py
          - README.md
          - agents.md
          - changelog.d/6785-check-triage-pr-head-routing.md
    - In scripts/check_failure_triage.sh, read `CHECK_TRIAGE_PR_HEAD_ROUTING_ENABLED` with default `false`. When it is not `true`, current behaviour is unchanged byte for byte.
    - When the flag is `true`, use the PR read the helper already makes. Routing requires all of these:
      - the PR is open;
      - the head repository equals the base repository;
      - the head ref passes `git check-ref-format --branch`;
      - the check-run head SHA and the PR head SHA are both nonempty and equal.
    - If any condition fails or can't be read, the helper:
      - logs `CHECK_TRIAGE ... outcome=skip reason=routing_unverified`;
      - sends a WARNING Telegram alert (fail-open);
      - exits 0 without filing an issue.
    - Once routing is verified, the script (not the model) appends `Integration branch: <head_ref>` to the composed body before the existing final body validation. That validation accepts exactly one such line, and only when it equals the verified head ref; any other routing line is still rejected.
    - In .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml, pass `CHECK_TRIAGE_PR_HEAD_ROUTING_ENABLED: ${{ vars.CHECK_TRIAGE_PR_HEAD_ROUTING_ENABLED || 'false' }}` through `env:` to the collect and diagnose steps. Never interpolate the head ref into `run:` source.
    - Add tests in tests/test_check_failure_triage_workflow_security.py:
      - flag off: no change;
      - accepted: open same-repo PR with matching SHAs;
      - rejected cases: fork head, closed PR, invalid ref, SHA mismatch, empty SHA, and a forged or duplicate `Integration branch:` line in model text.
    - Document the variable in README.md and the check-failure-triage entry in agents.md, and add the changelog fragment.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: none
  equivalence_argument: Option A gives the guard the exact trusted allowlist it was missing in #6785, with no globs. It covers the two automation paths and the ordinary files the general guard checks once a list exists.
  reversibility: The flag defaults to `false`, so turning it off (or never setting the repo variable) restores today's behaviour. The grant only allows the listed paths, and a person can narrow it by editing the issue body before `/approved`.

SETUP REQUIRED (only when a decision relies on a placeholder):
- FILES_TOUCHED_GRANT (resource): this needs a person. An OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, or the pipeline account, must edit the body of this issue and add the exact `files_touched:` block above before implement runs. I can't edit the issue body, and a block posted in a comment is not read. Until the block is there, implement's automation-path guard rejects the `scripts/` and `.github/` edits again and the issue returns to `ai:scope-blocked`.
- CHECK_TRIAGE_PR_HEAD_ROUTING_ENABLED (variable): set it to `true` per repository only after the change merges and has been reviewed. Until then the helper treats it as `false`, routes nothing, and files triage issues exactly as it does today.

Assumptions: This issue keeps its pipeline or trusted author, so a `files_touched` block added later still counts as trusted under the existing author check.

Missing context: I didn't have #6785's original description; this answer relies on the unblock judge's summary in this issue.
